To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a series of rare earth complexes RE(TPP) (acac) ( RE=NdIII, LuIII, Yb III, EuIII, PrIII, ErIII ) were prepared and characterized.
a rare earth metal complex RE(TPP)(Acac) (RE = Lu) was synthesized and its catalytic activity for the transformation of CO2 into cyclic carbonate was investigated.
the rare earth metal complex Lu(TPP)acac is an efficient catalyst for the synthesis of cyclic carbonate from CO2 and PO under mild conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of rare earth metal complex catalysts for the synthesis of cyclic carbonate from carbon dioxide and epoxide under mild conditions.
the development of rare earth metal porphyrin catalysts for CO2 fixation.
the development of a series of rare earth porphyrin complex catalysts, which can be used for the synthesis of cyclic carbonate under mild conditions without using co-solvent and co-catalysts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Lu(TPP)(H2O)2 is a promising catalyst for the cyclocarbonation of propylene oxide and CO2 under mild conditions.
the rare earth metal complexes are effective catalysts for the synthesis of cyclic carbonate from CO2 and propylene oxide.
the rare earth metal complexes can effectively catalyse the synthesis of cyclic carbonate under mild conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complex RE(TPP)(Acac) can be used as a promising catalyst for the synthesis of cyclic carbonate under mild conditions.
the catalytic activity of rare earth metal porphyrin catalysts is related to the metal ion radius, and the smaller the ion radius, the better the catalytic activity.

Lu(TPP)(H2O)2 is a highly active catalyst for the synthesis of cyclic carbonate under mild conditions without co-solvent, which could be a promising candidate for the large-scale production of cyclic carbonates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the catalytic reaction of Lu(TPP)(AcAc) could be completed within 2 h under mild conditions (40 °C and 0.5 MPa) with a high conversion of propylene oxide (99%) and a high yield of cyclic carbonates (98%).

the catalytic reactivities of the RE(TPP)(OAc) complexes were found to follow the order: Lu(TPP)(OAC) > Nd(TPP)(Oac) > Er(TPP)(Oa) > Yb(TPP)(Oc) > Pr(TPP)(Od) > Eu(TPP)(Oe), which was in agreement with the ionic radius of RE(III) ions.
Lu(TPP)(Acac) can catalyze the reaction of CO2 and propylene oxide to form propylene carbonate under atmospheric CO2 pressure at room temperature.
